newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel re-opens repaired south tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel re-opens repaired south tunnel.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc has re-opened its south rail tunnel after completing repairs following a severe blaze last November which caused 200 million pounds ($326.3 million) of damage and put 30 lorry drivers into hospital.

Just one day after the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority slammed Eurotunnel for its handling of safety after the fire, the group reported repairs to the tunnel had been completed on schedule. It was officially re-opened by joint chairman Patrick Ponsolle. Tunnel repairs cost 38 million pounds, which was covered by insurance.
"The re-opening of the tunnel has taken place on the date that we announced in January and the cost of the repairs is within the planned budget," Ponsolle said at the opening.

The group cleaned out the tunnel, removed damaged equipment and completed civil engineering work by March 28. This was followed by fitting electro-mechanical equipment including signalling, track and communications.

A tourist shuttle ran the length of the tunnel earlier on Wednesday. But Eurotunnel's freight services cannot resume until it gets the all-clear from the Intergovernmental Commission which is considering the Safety Authority's report this week.
A decision from the Commission could come as early as Thursday, say industry sources.

The ban on freight services followed the outbreak of a fire on a freight train wagon last November. Although Tuesday's safety report did not require a redesign of the open-sided freight wagons, controversy rages as fire chiefs claim the wagons are not safe.
